key_insight: The paper shows that quantum LDPC encoder circuits can be substantially improved by resynthesizing the encoder's CNOT matrix with a noise-aware, two-sided Hamming descent optimizer.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware teams, this offers a compiler-level way to reduce encoder gate count, routing depth, and state-preparation failure without changing the underlying code.
method: Treat LDPC encoder preparation as a circuit-resynthesis problem for the linear-reversible CNOT block.
Use two-sided Hamming descent to search for lower-cost equivalent encoders.
Select and schedule circuits with hardware noise and routing constraints in mind.
evidence_signal: Across CSS LDPC benchmarks, the pipeline cuts gate counts by 53.8% overall, up to 68% for Bivariate Bicycle codes, and reduces routed two-qubit depth by up to 71%.
watch_item: The gains depend on hardware-calibrated routing and scheduling, so performance may vary across devices and noise models.
paper_title: Noise-Aware Synthesis of Quantum LDPC Encoder Circuits via Two-Sided Hamming Descent
